title: Halima will lend you money
body: Halima Yusuf calls. She'll lend up to $500 at 15% a year — better than any bank will give you right now. She says she's heard good things and that her door is open once. She means it.

choices.label: Thank her and decline for now.

title: Miss Paula knows someone moving stock cheap
body: Miss Paula from two doors down says her nephew needs to clear phone cases and charging cables before he leaves for England. Everything goes at 60% of market. You'd need $200 to clear the lot. Could flip them on the market in a week.

title: Laptop for sale — owner needs quick cash
body: Someone in a WhatsApp group is selling a barely-used laptop for $180. They say it boots fine and they need rent money. Market price is closer to $350. No warranty, cash only, pickup in Half Way Tree today.

choices.label: Buy it for $180 and flip it.

title: Miss Enid is starting a Partner
body: Miss Enid is organising a Partner hand — 10 people, $50 each week. You draw in 8 weeks. That's $500 in one shot. Miss Enid has run it for 20 years without missing a draw. The commitment is $50 a week until your draw comes.

title: Western Union float hustle
body: Your friend Clive says there's good money helping families collect remittances from Toronto and New York without waiting in the Western Union line. You run the errand, take 3%. First week you could clear $80.

title: Limited Jordans below cost
body: A girl in your area needs cash today. She'll sell her boyfriend's boxfresh Jordans for $90. They'll go for $200 on Facebook Marketplace by the weekend. Cash in hand before noon.

title: Miss Clarke needs her yard painted
body: Miss Clarke up the road is repainting her fence and two exterior walls before her son's graduation. She'll pay $150 for the job. You'll need a weekend, two cans of paint from Budget Hardware, and someone to help.

choices.label: Too much work for the pay.

title: Bookkeeping offer — Spanish Town Road
body: Clive's uncle runs a wholesale business on Spanish Town Road. He needs weekly accounts. He'll pay $120 a week but wants to see you know what you're doing. If your numbers are good he'll recommend you to two other shops.
